summary: The core is one flat module (ckong.vhd) driven by an H/V raster counter (video_gen.vhd). It works as a scan-time pipeline: the low H-counter bits step a 16-slot fetch sequence, sprites are fetched during the H-blank part of each line into a line buffer that is cleared as it is read, and the big sprite is shifted out per pixel from its own X counter. None of it reproduces MAME's screen_update / tilemap / draw_sprites structure. Address quirks (A5 missing on the 98xx/9Cxx RAM) are built as wiring rather than as MAME's mirroring write handler, and the sample player uses a loadable counter instead of MAME's timer. It is not decomposed per chip and leaves out several board features, so it is hardware-leaning rather than strongly hardware-structured.

findings.note: addr_state, sprite index, tile X/Y and pixel X/Y all come straight from hcnt/vcnt bits (is_sprite = not hcnt(8), sprite = hcnt(6..4)). The H counter reloads to 128 and runs to 511, like a preloaded counter chain. Nothing is drawn per frame.

findings.signal: A5 not connected as address wiring
findings.note: CPU addresses in 9800-9FFF drop A5 when forming the RAM address (cpu_addr(10..6) & cpu_addr(4..0)). The video color fetch uses x_pixel(1) & y_tile(4..1) & x_tile. MAME instead models this with a write handler that duplicates the byte into both halves.

findings.signal: per-line sprite line buffer filled during H-blank
findings.note: Each line, the 8 sprites are fetched during the non-display half of the H count and written into a 256-entry line RAM. The RAM is read and cleared to zero while the background displays, and a sprite pixel already in the buffer is not overwritten. MAME uses a back-to-front loop over spriteram with transpen; the core reaches the same priority with a different mechanism.
Sprite Y matching is y_line + y_sprite + 1 with a test that the top nibble is 1111. That is an adder-and-carry comparator form, not MAME's y = 240 - spriteram[offs+2] screen-coordinate maths.

findings.signal: graphics ROM address assembled from counter bits
findings.note: The tile/sprite ROM address is built bit by bit: code, y_add bits (inverted for flip-Y), the x_tile(0) xor flipX half-select and y_pixel. This is how a 16x16 sprite is fetched as two 8-pixel halves on consecutive slots, instead of using a gfx-decode element.

findings.signal: big sprite as a per-pixel counter and shift pipeline
findings.note: The big sprite has its own preloadable X counter (x_big_sprite_counter). Its upper bits select the tile in 8800 RAM, its low bits select the pixel from two staged graphics registers, and a window compare gates it. The constants (172 - x) differ from MAME's control[3]-8 tilemap scroll.

findings.signal: sample rate as a reloading counter
findings.note: The sample clock comes from an 8-bit counter that reloads frequency_div when it overflows, clocked at 750 kHz, which is the TTL counter form. MAME schedules a timer at 256 - rate. The core also differs in nibble order and in holding (not looping) at the 0x70 end marker.

The interrupt is a latch set at a decoded raster line (y_tile=28, y_pixel=0) and held clear while the latch bit at A000 is low, like a flip-flop with an async clear, rather than a pulse on a VBLANK callback.

findings.signal: memory map, tile code bank bits, sample start*64
findings.note: Register addresses (A000/A800/B000/B800), colorram bits 4/5 as code bits 9/8, and the 0x70 end marker with start*64 must match any correct implementation.

findings.signal: FPGA SRAM time-multiplex and PROMs loaded into BRAM
findings.note: The 16-slot arbitration of one shared RAM for CPU and video, and the palettes loaded into BRAM, are FPGA resource choices.

Everything is in one module with abstract names (x_tile, addr_state), not chip or net names. Column scroll, screen flip, BG tile flip and the big-sprite priority bit are not implemented. That weakens the hardware case, but none of it points to MAME either.
